name: Kubernetes
description: Register Kubernetes clusters and give agents scoped, human-approved access to them through an mcp__cockpit-k8s__* server. The plugin talks to the cluster itself (via the official Kubernetes client) and keeps the credentials — an agent never gets a kubeconfig. Every call is gated: opening a cluster asks for consent, a namespace outside the cluster's allowed list asks each session (reads included), and every change asks afresh and is never remembered. Cluster-scoped resources, exec and port-forward are off until you turn them on per cluster. A port-forward tunnel shows in the status bar with an operator-only Kill and auto-closes. Helm releases can be read (helm_list/helm_status/helm_history/helm_values/helm_manifest) straight from their release secrets, no helm binary needed, and get_resource flags a resource as Helm-managed — installed when the release annotations are there, or just rendered without an install (e.g. by Argo CD's `helm template`) when they are not, so an Argo-managed resource carrying Helm's label is no longer misreported as an installed release. helm_rollback rolls a release back to an earlier revision by applying the manifest that revision stored, and helm_upgrade upgrades a release by rendering the chart with a helm dry run and applying that; both put the literal manifest diff on the approval, are deliberately not full helm parity (no three-way merge, no hooks), and there is no install or uninstall. Argo CD's GitOps state can be read straight from its Application CRD, no Argo token or binary needed: argo_apps lists an Application's sync status/health/sourceType/revision, argo_app unpacks one Application including whether auto-sync/selfHeal are on, argo_history lists its deployed revisions, and argo_last_sync shows what the last sync did per resource. get_resource also flags a resource as Argo-managed (the owning Application, read off its tracking-id annotation or, for a real Argo label-tracking setup and not merely a Helm chart that also sets it, the instance label) — when a resource is owned by both Argo CD and Helm, Argo is reported as the owner and Helm as at most its renderer. An optional, per-cluster Argo CD API token (a read-only project-role token, pasted in the plugin settings and kept under the secret layer, same as the kubeconfig) lets the plugin reach Argo's own REST API through the kube-apiserver's service proxy — no ingress, no tunnel, and the token never appears in a consent card, an error, or cockpit.json. argo_refresh asks Argo CD to re-read Git and refresh an Application's status now — it sets a refresh annotation on the Application itself, which Argo CD removes once it has reconciled, and rolls out, updates or deletes no resource; its approval prompt is gated on its own scope, not the one a real cluster change asks through. Configure clusters in the plugin settings: point at a kubeconfig file (e.g. ~/.kube/config, read live) and pick a context from it, or paste a kubeconfig which is stored under the secret layer.
author: Cockpit
